observedCustomerOutcome: At mobile 390px and desktop 1440px, the initial web-only owner sees all four service cards and all four visible choices, with unselected status and useful Choose actions.
Choose phone changes only the local draft. Save choices and reload retain web plus voice without authorizing or activating service.

Review phone details opens the existing canonical contact section and focuses the missing business-line field. The owner saves a separate business line, carrier and all-call forwarding choice through the actual PUT handler, while reusing the saved separate owner contact cell.
Ordinary business-details Save then Connections, without reload, retains all four cards and current next actions; a later reload retains the phone facts and service choices.

The shared business review works through its actual handler. After review, unavailable AI practice is shown as Waiting for AI service for phone and texting; no number reservation or service success is inferred.
SMS and Calendar choices save incrementally. Calendar separately explains that Google approval will be requested when available. Selection does not perform OAuth or provider work.
Inbox and Schedule actions open the actual request and saved-visit screens. The text distinguishes saved records from delivered messages and synced visits.
The website editor has exactly one visible Save website and one Cancel. The ordinary Add website action opens it, and the actual website PUT saves and reuses the canonical URL.

Current mobile and desktop screens fit their viewport. Unsupported managed-call transfer and backup urgent-alert fields remain hidden; the visible fallback explanation correctly names the saved owner contact cell.

Supplementary independent QA establishes the available-offer and recovery states: current costs/legal/consent decisions, safe forwarding choice, Calendar start interception, retained permissions, no new number offer for web/Calendar-only selections, retained number cancellation, error/slow/lost-response recovery and keyboard focus.
